title: Aerospace Propulsion Engineer
description: About this positionIn a world where access to advanced propulsion technologies is increasingly important for security and strategic autonomy, you will directly contribute to innovations that strengthen Europe’s technological capabilities. You will work on solutions that go beyond the drawing board and are actually developed, tested, and validated. Are you ready to help shape the next generation of aerospace propulsion technologies? Then we would love to hear from you.What will be your role?As an aerospace propulsion engineer, you will collaborate closely with the Aerospace Propulsion team to design and analyse key components and technologies of propulsion systems, including combustion chambers, air intakes, propellant and fuel formulations, gas generators and propellant feed systems. Working alongside experienced engineers and scientists, you will be involved in the full chain of technology development, from initial concept generation to prototype fabrication and performance evaluation. Your responsibilities will also include developing comprehensive test plans, selecting appropriate measurement techniques, and actively participating in the execution of tests in TNO’s Propulsion Test Facility. This will entail preparing experimental setups, conducting data acquisition, and performing post-test analyses of the test data. By actively participating in design and experimental work, you will help drive advancements in aerospace propulsion technologies within a multidisciplinary team. You will also present findings to stakeholders and collaborate on research publications.You will become part of the Aerospace Propulsion (AP) team within the Department of Energetic Systems (ES). The department of Energetic Systems is dedicated to advancing research in energetic materials and their applications in both the defence and civilian domain. It manages all aspects related to energetic materials, including synthesis, production, processing, and characterization, as well as the analysis and design of associated systems. The department employs approximately 40 professionals with backgrounds in engineering, chemistry, and physics. The Aerospace Propulsion team, one of the department's specialized groups, focuses on developing innovative technologies for aerospace propulsion applications, such as rockets, ramjets, and rotating detonation engines. Comprised of approximately ten engineers and scientists, the team utilizes state-of-the-art modelling and simulation tools and test facilities to rigorously evaluate the propulsion technologies developed.What we expect from youWe are looking for a highly motivated and dependable professional who enjoys working in a team-oriented setting. The ideal candidate will be able to handle their own tasks independently, make smart choices when planning tasks, and working within multiple projects at the same time. Dedication to developing creative technical solutions and contributing to a safer society is important. When unexpected challenges arise, you should be able to adapt quickly and collaborate with your team to find effective solutions. Strong attention to details and the ability to keep sight of big-picture project goals are both crucial.You also bring:PhD or MSc in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, (applied) physics, or related field;Strong interest in aerospace and defence;Knowledge of (aero-)thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, combustion and aerospace propulsion.Candidates with limited domain-specific knowledge should have at least five years of relevant work experience in an engineering capacity;Experience with MATLAB and/or Python;Any prior exposure to designing and testing aerospace propulsion systems or components is appreciated, but not required;Any knowledge of the production process of solid rocket propellants and/or solid fuels would be considered advantageous, but is not mandatory.Good commandment of the Dutch and English language, both verbally and in writing.What you'll get in returnChallenging and varied work with a real impact. And plenty of opportunities as, at TNO, you are in charge of shaping your career. We offer a gross monthly salary between € 3,530 and € 6,884 (based on your knowledge and experience), 8% holiday pay, a 13th month bonus of 8.33% and a flex budget (5.58% + € 180). In addition, you will be given every opportunity to develop yourself.Perhaps you would like to grow your career in the direction of commerce or consultancy? Or would you like to become a project manager? Immerse yourself in sustainable innovations? Or carve out a career as a technical expert?TNO offers optional employee benefits, enabling you to tailor your benefits package to match your personal situation. You may also expect:An extremely professional, innovative working environment where colleagues are leading experts in their field.The opportunity to attend courses, workshops and conferences, and to receive training and coaching based on your needs.33 days annual leave plus a flexible holiday that can be used on a cultural, religious, or otherwise important day of your choosing (on a full-time basis).An employer working towards a respectful, inclusive, and equitable work environment where every employee can flourish, with various initiatives such as Jong TNO, numerous expertise based guilds, Rainbow Community and Round Tables on diverse inclusion topics.We offer a comprehensive and flexible mobility plan that also includes full compensation for public transportation for commuting and business travel.Great social events with your team and other TNO colleagues. That’s how you will get to know a lot of people really quickly.Flexible working hours, the possibility to work parttime (32 or 36 hours) and the possibility of working from home.Extensive relocation package for international candidates.A good pension scheme.Read more about tailoring your benefits package.TNO as an employerOur people are at the heart of TNO. Their curiosity, expertise and entrepreneurial mindset make it possible to deliver high-impact research and innovations that contribute to society’s sustainable wellbeing and prosperity. That is why we invest in an inspiring and inclusive working environment where colleagues can excel, have autonomy and continue to grow.Your talent and ambition have every opportunity to flourish at TNO. You work with experts (both within and beyond TNO), have access to advanced technology and the freedom to explore, experiment and innovate. Our strength lies in independence, reliability and collaboration. We find each other in wonder and ingenuity. We are driven to push boundaries. By working with businesses and government, and by connecting different perspectives, we strengthen our innovative capability and create responsible, meaningful results.At TNO, we believe this is our time to help society, government and business move forward faster. Together with driven colleagues, you turn knowledge into concrete innovations or ventures that truly make a difference by combining the power of science and entrepreneurship. And in doing so, you make your mark on our time.The selection processPlease apply before the 15th of October, 2026. The selection process comprises two interview rounds. In a final meeting we will discuss the terms of employment and your tailored benefits package. We aim to finalize the entire process within four weeks.The selection process may include an online assessment and a reference check.As you will be working for clients in the domain of defence and security, a Certificate of No Objection issued by AIVD (the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service) is mandatory. description: About this positionSafety and security cannot be taken for granted. Sometimes, you have to fight for peace. There is always a frontline somewhere, where history is being written. The impact on our armed forces of rising tensions around the world, especially the ongoing struggle over Ukraine, is huge. The knowledge and technology needs of our founding partner, the Dutch Ministry of Defence, are evolving faster and changing, the pace is accelerating, and research and development budgets are growing rapidly. In line with this, the focus on our national, domestic security is also intensifying, for instance in the fight against worsening drug-related crime in the Netherlands. This is where knowledge and technology make the difference, and we translate that into our mission!The Compact Radar Systems research group is part of the Defence, Safety & Security (DSS) unit, which houses a total of 23 research groups in 5 divisions.The Compact Radar Systems research group is 1 of 6 research groups within the Electromagnetics & Military Operations division. The research group has three main topics: RF applications in space, radar on flying platforms for ISR purposes such as SAR and autonomous flight applications, and cost effective effectors. The expertisgroup currently consists of 30 professionals with expertise related to radar system development, system engineering, algorithm development, signal processing, analogue- and digital high frequency electronics. The group has an international character, with English and Dutch as the working languages.What will be your role?You will be running the Compact Radar Systems research group together with the Research Manager. As the group’s manager, you will be close to our researchers, know the broad strokes of what they are working on, and be able to create the ideal framework conditions for them to perform optimally. title: Internship | Agent-based modelling of bird migration through wind farms
description: About this positionTwice a year, once in Spring and once in Summer, millions of songbirds traverse the Netherlands during their seasonal migration. As offshore wind energy is rapidly expanding, migratory birds may fly in proximity to wind turbines, thereby facing an increased risk of collision. If we can successfully simulate birds flying through offshore wind farms, we can improve predictions of collision risks during these mass migration events and/or improve wind farm layouts and operations to reduce those risks.What will be your role?At TNO, we are developing an agent-based model to simulate the flight of migratory birds through offshore wind farms. The model aims to capture a range of behaviours, from macro-avoidance of entire wind farms to micro-avoidance and collision risk at the level of individual turbines. In this project you will further adapt this agent-based model to (1) simulate bird flight behaviour as realistically as possible based on actual measurements, and (2) use the model to test how different wind farm layouts affect predicted collision risks. title: Internship | Design of phased array in E-Band for future SATCOM applications
description: About this positionFuture satellite communication systems need to transmit increasingly large amounts of data. Moving towards higher frequencies, such as E-band, can provide the required capacity, but it also creates new challenges for antenna design. The antennas must generate highly directional beams, scan over a wide angular range and operate efficiently despite the losses associated with these frequencies.This internship focuses on the development of a novel antenna array for future E-band satellite communication systems. You will work with our antenna research team to investigate different array technologies and identify promising solutions for efficient, wide-angle beam scanning. Your work will contribute to the development of advanced antenna systems that can support future high-capacity satellite links.You will be part of a collaborative research environment where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcomed and you will have the opportunity to further develop your expertise in antenna design and electromagnetic simulation.What will be your role?During this internship, you will investigate and compare different phased-array antenna technologies suitable for E-band satellite communications. You will assess their expected performance and explore the main trade-offs related to efficiency, scanning range, complexity and practical implementation.Based on this analysis, you will select one or more promising concepts and design antenna elements that can operate efficiently while supporting a wide beam-scanning range. You will use electromagnetic software simulators (e.g. Ansys HFSS or CST studio suite) to model, simulate and optimize the proposed designs.The internship will include different phases, such as:Reviewing relevant antenna-array technologies and design approaches;Defining performance requirements and comparison criteria;Modelling and comparing suitable array concepts;Designing and optimizing wide-scanning antenna elements in CST;Evaluating parameters such as efficiency, impedance matching, radiation pattern and scanning performance;Documenting the results and presenting recommendations for further development.The exact focus of the assignment can be refined together based on your interests, background and the results obtained during the first stages of the internship.By the end of the internship, you will have developed practical experience in antenna-array design, electromagnetic simulation, technical decision-making and the communication of research results. Your findings will support the selection and development of antenna technologies for future satellite communication systems. This internship is in the framework of a project between TNO and Viasat.What we expect from youFor this internship, we are looking for a university student pursuing a M.Sc. degree with a background in electrical engineering, telecommunications, applied physics or a related discipline. title: Internship | Knowledge Graphs for Infrastructure Renewal
description: About this positionThis internship offers the opportunity to contribute to innovative research at the intersection of Knowledge Graphs and emerging technologies, with the goal of improving data-driven decision-making in complex infrastructure environments. You will work on challenges related to integrating and structuring information from diverse data sources, enabling organizations to make better-informed, more transparent, and explainable decisions throughout the asset management lifecycle.As part of a multidisciplinary team, you will investigate how Knowledge Graphs can be combined with complementary technologies such as machine learning, large language models, computer vision, or geospatial analytics to create intelligent solutions for real-world problems. The position combines scientific research with practical experimentation, including literature studies, data analysis, prototype development, and evaluation. Throughout the internship, you will have the freedom to explore a research direction that matches your interests and expertise while contributing to the development of innovative methods for knowledge integration, decision support, and infrastructure intelligence. Ideas are welcomed, and you have the space to develop your expertise.What will be your role?During this internship, you will work on exploring and developing methods to integrate Knowledge Graphs with technologies to address real-world infrastructure renewal challenges. You will have the flexibility to focus on a specific research direction that aligns with your interests and academic background.Research directions:AI Agents and Knowledge GraphsExplore how LLM based agents can use Knowledge Graphs to carry out infrastructure assessment tasks, such as finding and combining relevant information, using existing engineering rules and calculations, identifying missing information, and explaining assessment results.Advanced Engineering Reasoning and Knowledge GraphsExplore how Knowledge Graphs can support increasingly detailed engineering assessments by incorporating more expressive rules, calculations and degradation models. The research will also include developing and testing a prototype using relevant tools, frameworks, and datasets, evaluating its practical applicability, explainability, and value for decision support, and documenting key findings, lessons learned, and recommendations for future research and implementation.What we expect from youFor this internship, we are looking for a master’s student with a background in STEM such as civil engineering, mechanical engineering, architecture, (applied) physics or mathematics, computer science, or similar. Using these technologies, you will design, characterize, and simulate components, perform circuit and electromagnetic (EM) simulations, and optimize layouts.
